clue.text: Fellow about to move initially with bishop in neat sacrifice

parts.note: a fellow is a he, a man
CA, circa, is Latin shorthand for about
taken as written

indicators.note: initially asks for only the opening letter of the word move

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: Someone shifts with a bishop during a tidy ritual offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat' is not tidy: it is the old word for cattle, and a hecatomb was a sacrifice of a hundred oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was a great public offering of cattle, originally a hundred oxen, so it is a sacrifice of neat.

clue.text: Writing report to express appreciation

definitions.note: the clue reads as a thing used to express appreciation, a noun

parts.note: one's hand is one's handwriting
a clap is a loud report, as of thunder

explanation.surface: Composing a write-up to show thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A single strike of the palms together is applause, the usual sign of approval.

clue.text: Intrigued when prisoner observed to pocket rasp initially

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner

indicators.note: to pocket means the observing word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: spied means observed

indicators.note: initially asks for only the first letter of the word rasp

explanation.surface: A convict watched by guards plots to hide a file.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrigued in its older sense means plotted secretly, schemed.

clue.text: Test for fitness to proceed with trial

parts.note: a try is an attempt or trial
on means forward, as in go on

explanation.surface: A medical examination before being allowed to continue with an experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A try-on is when one puts on clothes to see whether they fit.

clue.text: Pungent extract from Grimm — or Dante?

indicators.note: extract from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A biting passage taken from fairy tales or the Inferno.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is sharp and biting, just as a pungent remark stings.

clue.text: Bringer of fortune for many a Northerner?

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, standing for many
taken as written
a Scot comes from the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A question whether lots of northern folk bring good luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a charm or creature kept for the good luck it is thought to bring.

clue.text: Curiously not a rich quarter for one seeking privacy

indicators.note: curiously means the letters of not a rich come out in an odd order

parts.note: E, east, is one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Strangely, a poor district suits a recluse.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchorite is a hermit who withdraws from the world to live alone.

clue.text: Carpentier oddly selected for development of Mediterranean island

indicators.note: oddly selected asks for the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the name

explanation.surface: A boxer named for building up a holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: CARPENTIER is Georges Carpentier, the French boxer; the OCR copy misread it as Carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Crete is the largest Greek island, in the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Attractive business income cut short

indicators.note: cut short means the word for receipts loses its last letter

parts.note: a shop's takings are its income

explanation.surface: Appealing profits, but trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking in the old sense means charming or captivating.

clue.text: Finish or start watch?

definitions.meaning: to bring to a close, to conclude
to turn the key of a clockwork watch to set it going

explanation.definitionFit: To wind up is to conclude something, and also to tighten a watch spring so it runs.

clue.text: Protector of girl in New York

indicators.note: in places the girl's name inside the letters for the city

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone who guards a young woman living in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A nanny looks after and safeguards children in her care, acting as their guardian.

clue.text: Hurried inspection involving individual's certificate of insurance

indicators.note: involving means the first word takes the single letter within it

parts.note: hurried means ran
I, the single figure one, stands for an individual
an inspection is a check

explanation.surface: A rushed examination of a person's insurance paperwork.
explanation.definitionFit: A rain check is a ticket guaranteeing a later chance if an event is rained off, a form of insurance voucher.

clue.text: Humbly soliciting Crown and getting attention

parts.note: a cap covers the crown of the head, and a crown on a tooth is a cap
a matter in hand is being attended to

explanation.surface: Begging the monarchy for notice in a lowly manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Going about with one's hat held before one is the image of someone begging meekly.

clue.text: No prison in which to hold East Indian, for example

parts.note: O, zero, means none at all

indicators.note: in which to hold means the prison word keeps the compass letter within it

parts.note: can is slang for prison
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A man from the east is held without any jail to keep him in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person from the East; it is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one of the world's great seas, along with the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: A tumbler easily overturned

parts.note: reads as a drinking glass knocked over without effort, but describes a gymnast who flips head over heels with ease

explanation.surface: A drinking glass that falls over at the slightest knock.
explanation.definitionFit: A circus performer who turns somersaults and handsprings is a tumbler going head over heels with practised ease.

clue.text: Bachelor found on every top establishment on the Strand

parts.note: each means every
the head is the top

explanation.surface: A single man running a business in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: The Strand looks like the famous London street; read it as a strand, a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A beachhead is a position secured by invading troops on a shore.

clue.text: Cardinals perhaps working in post

indicators.note: working means the letters of in post are set to work in a new order

explanation.surface: Senior churchmen busy at their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Cardinals look like churchmen, but here they are the cardinal compass directions.
explanation.definitionFit: North, south, east and west are the cardinal compass points.

clue.text: Proof of ownership — let it resolve the action

indicators.note: resolve means the letters of let it are broken up and reset

parts.note: a deed is an action

explanation.surface: A deed settling who owns a property in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A title deed is the legal document showing who holds a property.

clue.text: Fragment offered to journalist taken with alacrity

parts.note: a snatch is a short fragment, as of song
ED, editor, is the standard crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A scrap of news given to a reporter is grabbed eagerly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something snatched is grabbed quickly and eagerly.

clue.text: Potential customers these days get service

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era
a mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Modern shoppers expecting to be served.
explanation.definitionFit: Admass is the mass public targeted by advertising, the potential buyers it aims at.

clue.text: Pull out all the stops for the melody

definitions.meaning: to make the greatest possible effort

explanation.definitionFit: To strain is to exert oneself to the utmost, and a strain is a passage of music.

clue.text: Quiet break before performing in Lancashire

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
a break is a rest
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: An actor takes a quiet pause before going on stage up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' simply orders the pieces. LANCASHIRE is an English county in the north-west.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition names the place by location: a town found within that north-western county.

clue.text: Public notice presaging new access

indicators.note: presaging means the notice comes before the next piece

parts.note: a poster is a notice put up in public

explanation.surface: A billboard announcing a new entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate giving entry to a castle.

clue.text: Part of the circle showing no tact when wrong

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of no tact are put out of order

explanation.surface: Part of a social set behaving tactlessly when in error.
explanation.definitionFit: An octant is one eighth of a circle, a 45-degree sector.

clue.text: Clergy drawing many into church

indicators.note: into means the word for many goes inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Priests attracting a crowd into their place of worship.
explanation.definitionFit: The cloth is a collective name for priests and ministers, from their distinctive dress.

clue.text: Perfume of repute

definitions.meaning: standing, as in being in good or bad favour with someone

explanation.definitionFit: Odour means a smell, and in phrases like in good odour it means reputation.

clue.text: Quick to recover the right to enter second examination

indicators.note: to enter means the right goes inside the word for the retaken exam

parts.note: a resit is an exam taken a second time
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A student bounces back, entitled to sit the test again.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resilient springs back quickly after hardship or illness.

clue.text: Volume containing story about right in the ascendant

indicators.note: about means the story wraps around the next piece

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story

indicators.note: in the ascendant means rising, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

explanation.surface: A book holding a tale about a rising right-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: A litre is a metric measure of capacity, so a volume.

clue.text: Pay for back issue simultaneously

parts.note: to atone is to pay for a wrong

indicators.note: back means the word for issue is read from end to start

parts.note: to issue is to emit

explanation.surface: Paying for an old edition of a magazine all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Things happening together occur at the same moment, which is what the phrase can mean.

clue.text: Driving area used by most of the force

parts.note: the tee is where a golfer drives from

indicators.note: most of means the word the loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A golf tee used by most of the police.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real power to compel; teeth means effective power.

clue.text: Lecture for one going into business

indicators.note: going into means the numeral enters the word for business

parts.note: trade is business
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A talk for someone starting a commercial career.
explanation.definitionFit: A tirade is a long angry speech, a harangue or scolding.

clue.text: Elected, and nursed constituents as planned

parts.note: a politician elected to office is in
tended means looked after, as an MP nurses a constituency

explanation.surface: Voted in and cared for the voters, just as arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: What is intended is meant or designed in advance, deliberate.
